paragraphs.text: The method was boring to perform: I copied each handwritten address onto a separate card for the entire afternoon. The task required no choices once the handwriting was legible, and I welcomed the tea break.
The better option became boring. Put the detachable handles in the same box as the pans, with a cloth between the metal surfaces to prevent scratches during transport.
The inventory audit was boring because every cabinet contained the same packets of blank forms. I still had to open each door and compare its contents with the stock sheet before signing the count.
This response is boring: send the applicant a copy of the decision and retain the original in the case folder. Use the address recorded on the application rather than the envelope.
This practical rule is boring. Return each borrowed costume on a hanger with its size label facing outward, and place loose accessories in the mesh bag attached to the hanger.
The actual strategy remains boring: alternate the beds planted with beans and onions between growing seasons. Keep a sketch of each bed's planting beside the seed envelopes in the potting shed.
The recommendation was boring: store the spare sails in canvas sleeves. We tried the arrangement during the winter layup and kept each sleeve on its own hook above the workbench.
The remedy remains boring. Replace the felt pads beneath the cabinet feet, then check that the doors close without scraping the frame before returning the dishes to the upper shelf.
This technique stays boring. Count the stitches at the end of each row and mark the count on the paper pattern before turning the fabric for the return row.
The remedy for damp cellars remains boring. Extend the drainpipe beyond the foundation and slope the surrounding soil away from the bricks, then inspect the corner after the next heavy rainfall.

The puppet show was boring; the narrator repeated every line after the puppets had spoken it, doubling each exchange without adding a joke. We left at the interval and walked back along the waterfront.

This better approach across the branch network is boring. Keep a duplicate bundle of requisition slips at each counter, and collect completed slips in the same tray before the evening delivery leaves.

The practical solution for cross-campus equipment bookings remains boring. In our fictional proposal, departments share a calendar and reserve microscopes through a common form. A facilities clerk checks the next morning's reservations before locking the stores.

The inventory count across the satellite depots was boring because it required reading identical serial prefixes aloud for every item. A barcode scan would have checked the same identifiers without the repetitive recitation. We requested scanners for the next count.

The comedy about the hotel kitchen is boring: every scene repeats the same mistaken order without changing the joke or the characters' responses. Even the final banquet repeats dialogue from the opening breakfast. The cast gets little new material to play.

In his draft, Pavel writes, "The practical remedy for shrinking audiences remains boring." His editor circles boring and asks him to name the remedy and its expected effect on ticket renewals. She deletes the sentence when he supplies neither.

The design team presented a cardboard model of the new parcel counter. But the right approach across the service network is boring. The model included a hinged flap and removable dividers for envelopes of different sizes.

The report on the canal restoration is boring because each chapter restates the project mandate before describing a single repair. Removing those repeated introductions would let readers compare the repairs without rereading the same paragraph eight times.
